title: supermarket/customers
description: One row per loyalty-card holder. Registered customers. Only loyalty-card holders appear here, so many transactions have no customer at all -- which is realistic and makes this a natural LEFT JOIN test case.

loyalty_card.description: The number printed on the physical loyalty card, which is what a cashier scans at the till.

full_name.description: Spanish name with both surnames, as it would be captured on a loyalty application form.

email.description: Contact address on the reserved example.com domain, with accents transliterated away. Empty for about 15% of customers who never supplied one.

phone.description: Mostly Spanish mobile numbers, since that is what people give a shop. Empty for around 9% of rows.

city.description: Spanish city of residence, which is usually but not always the city of the store they shop at.

province.description: Province of residence, consistent with the postal code in the next column.

postal_code.description: Spanish postal code whose first two digits are the province code, so address validation passes.

birth_date.description: Date of birth where the customer gave one, used for age-band marketing. Empty for about 20% of rows.

segment.description: Marketing segment derived from spend and visit frequency. Premium customers really do spend more per basket in this data, so the segmentation is worth plotting.

signed_up_at.description: Date the loyalty card was issued. Always on or before that customer's first transaction.
